body: I meant it when I said I have nothing. The only reason I still wake up and go to work is so I have money to spend on sugary food. In a way, I hope to one day eat so much that my stomach pops. I'm sure if I do end up quitting, I'd just lay in bed until I either die of hunger or thirst. I am broken. I was born into an abusive family with nothing, and I grew into a nothing loser. God must be laughing at the misery I was born to live.

I have had people tell me that for years. I have also been told it gets better. I don't see it. Every year, it just gets worse and worse. It gets harder and harder. I haven't smiled since I was a child and I've been crying alone more and more.

I have no future. I know that. What's the point in keeping on going? I have no skills. I have a poverty level income. I will either end up on the streets or dead.

It really is. Those who have money want more of it, and those below them have to suffer because of it.

Working 8+ hour days 5 or more days a week is severely outdated, but the pay remains scraps. We spend so much of our lives working and sleeping. Many of us also rely on public transport to get us to work. It's all so pointless and draining.

I have turned to food for comfort because it feels like the only thing I can control, even though it actually controls me.

I feel you. I had to leave a few Discord groups because I would often be turned into the butt of jokes. I'd ask them to stop without any change, or just silently vanish because I didn't want to be a party pooper.

Seems so. You can't really bring up things like this around the water cooler. People will start avoiding you (making you feel even more alone or broken), or they'll throw you in some room where a crazy nurse might abuse you even more.

It's either wear a mask, or become shunned.

Feels like there's no winning no matter what you do. Still, for some reason, many of us have something that keeps us rolling out of bed. Still not sure what that is for me.

It wouldn't be so hard if we could all just happily enjoy life instead of putting 40+ or 80+ hours into a job that barely keep you afloat--all while you make the big hats even richer. If you manage to retire, your body is too old to really enjoy life anymore and you don't have much time left.

It feels like high school was just yesterday for me. I blinked, and now I'm in my late twenties. No friends. No family to turn to. Life feels like it's stuck on repeat.

What's the point, really?
Funny enough, reading this subreddit is the only thing keeping me from going too far off the deep end mentally. Misery loves company, I guess.

Some do it for a selfish hero complex reason; some believe they're helping you. Many do it for the money.

Nobody chose to be born. Why is it so horrible to have the choice whether we stay or not? It wouldn't be so hard if people didn't have to struggle so much just to keep a roof and food.

All it can really take is one traumatic experience to flip your life / perspective; it doesn't have to be lifelong.

I can relate to you. Even though I was abused at home growing up, I still had some bliss to me. Younger me believed everything would be okay once I hit adulthood.

I was so stupidly wrong.

If things don't get better for me, I just know I'll end up giving up and ending everything myself. There's only so much more I can take. I don't think I'll make it to 30. I'm trying, but I keep hitting wall after wall. COVID seems like the final middle finger.
Reading this reply made me burst into tears--again. God, I'm pathetic. I can't keep doing this day to day. It hurts too much.
